triggered_rules.description: Archive contains executable or binary files.
triggered_rules.rationale: Executables bundled in archives are a primary delivery mechanism for malware; they bypass email attachment filters that block .exe directly.

triggered_rules.description: Archive contains script files that can execute OS commands.
triggered_rules.rationale: Script files (.ps1, .vbs, .bat, .sh …) execute with user-level privileges on double-click and are widely abused as first-stage loaders.

triggered_rules.description: Double-extension filenames disguise executables as documents.
triggered_rules.rationale: Windows hides known extensions by default; 'report.pdf.exe' displays as 'report.pdf', inducing the user to double-click and execute malware believing it is a document.

triggered_rules.description: Decoy document + executable — classic dropper pattern.
triggered_rules.rationale: Pairing a harmless-looking document with an executable is the hallmark of a dropper: the victim opens the document, sees expected content, and never notices the payload that ran in the background.

triggered_rules.description: Download-command keywords in strings — indicates staged malware delivery.
triggered_rules.rationale: Commands like Invoke-WebRequest, certutil -decode, or BITSAdmin are used by loaders to fetch a second-stage payload after the archive is extracted and executed.

triggered_rules.description: Shell-execution API references in strings — possible malicious script.
triggered_rules.rationale: WScript.Shell, CreateProcess, VirtualAlloc and similar APIs are core primitives for process spawning and code injection used by malware.

triggered_rules.description: High-entropy files (≥ 7.5 bits/byte) — likely packed or encrypted payloads.
triggered_rules.rationale: A Shannon entropy of ≥ 7.5 bits/byte indicates near-random data, consistent with encrypted or UPX/MPRESS-packed executables.  Legitimate plain-text files score 4–6.

triggered_rules.description: Phishing-related terms in filenames — social-engineering lure.
triggered_rules.rationale: Terms like 'invoice', 'payment', 'urgent', or 'verify' exploit psychological urgency to induce users to open archive contents without scrutiny.

triggered_rules.description: CVE-2023-38831 pattern: ZIP with same-named file+folder containing executable.
triggered_rules.evidence: Format: ZIP, Name collisions: [], Executables present.
triggered_rules.rationale: CVE-2023-38831 is a WinRAR logical flaw: when the user clicks a benign file, WinRAR also extracts and runs executables inside a same-named folder, achieving silent RCE.  Actively exploited by APT28, Sandworm, and others.

triggered_rules.description: Hardcoded URLs/IPs in strings — possible C2 channel or staged download.
triggered_rules.rationale: Hardcoded network addresses inside archive content indicate the extracted payload will phone home or pull a second stage from an attacker-controlled server.

triggered_rules.description: Extreme compression ratio — potential decompression bomb (zip-of-death).
triggered_rules.rationale: A decompression bomb (CWE-409) stores gigabytes or petabytes of data in a tiny file.  Extracting it exhausts disk/RAM and can crash or disable antivirus engines, creating an opening for secondary payloads. CVE-2019-9674 covers this class of attack in Python's zipfile module.

triggered_rules.description: CVE-2021-36090: High compression/file-count ZIP may cause Commons Compress OOM.
triggered_rules.rationale: CVE-2021-36090: Apache Commons Compress 1.0–1.20 allocates memory proportional to claimed (uncompressed) sizes in ZIP entries.  A crafted archive with huge claimed sizes causes OOM even for very small compressed inputs, crashing any Java service that processes the file.

triggered_rules.rationale: Recursive archives exhaust AV scan budgets; the inner payload is never inspected.  Depth ≥ 3 strongly suggests intentional evasion.

triggered_rules.description: Decoy document + executable — classic dropper pattern.
triggered_rules.rationale: Pairing a harmless-looking document with an executable is the hallmark of a dropper: the victim opens the document, sees expected content, and never notices the payload that ran in the background.

triggered_rules.description: High-entropy files (≥ 7.5 bits/byte) — likely packed or encrypted payloads.
triggered_rules.rationale: A Shannon entropy of ≥ 7.5 bits/byte indicates near-random data, consistent with encrypted or UPX/MPRESS-packed executables.  Legitimate plain-text files score 4–6.

triggered_rules.description: CVE-2023-38831 pattern: ZIP with same-named file+folder containing executable.
triggered_rules.evidence: Format: ZIP, Name collisions: [], Executables present.
triggered_rules.rationale: CVE-2023-38831 is a WinRAR logical flaw: when the user clicks a benign file, WinRAR also extracts and runs executables inside a same-named folder, achieving silent RCE.  Actively exploited by APT28, Sandworm, and others.
